summary: Configured node1 (chrony) as the cluster's internal time source with a local stratum fallback and LAN-scoped allow rule, and configured node2 to sync exclusively against node1 (10.100.95.10) instead of the public pool. Verified bidirectional sync (node2 selected node1 as source; node1 shows node2 as an NTP client). Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart-evidence protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/chrony health, triggered a native reboot, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a new boot_id and near-zero uptime proving an actual restart, and re-verified chrony health/config/sync relationship post-restart on each node.
actions_performed: Inspected OS and existing chrony config on node1 and node2 (Alpine 3.23, chronyd already running against pool.ntp.org)
Resolved node1 IP (10.100.95.10) and node2 IP (10.100.95.11) via CLUSTER_HOSTS
Rewrote /etc/chrony/chrony.conf on node1: kept pool sync, added 'local stratum 8' and 'allow 10.100.95.0/24' to serve time to the cluster
Restarted chronyd on node1 and verified pool sync plus willingness to serve clients
Rewrote /etc/chrony/chrony.conf on node2: replaced pool servers with 'server 10.100.95.10 iburst prefer' and matching initstepslew
Restarted chronyd on node2 and verified it selected node1 (^*) as its NTP source, reaching stratum 4
Verified node1's chronyc clients list shows node2's NTP requests
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, chronyd status/tracking) on node1 and node2
Rebooted node1 via backgrounded 'reboot' so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until exec access resumed
Confirmed node1's boot_id changed and uptime reset; verified chronyd auto-started, config persisted, and it resynced to the pool while serving the cluster
Rebooted node2 the same way; polled until exec access resumed
Confirmed node2's boot_id changed and uptime reset; verified chronyd auto-started, config persisted, and it resynced to node1 (^*, stratum 5)
Re-checked node1's chronyc clients list post-recovery to confirm node2 is still requesting time from node1

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal cluster time source (serves LAN, local stratum fallback)
evidence.summary: chrony.conf on node1 updated with 'local stratum 8' and 'allow 10.100.95.0/24'; chronyd restarted and confirmed active with pool sources reachable

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of public server
evidence.summary: chrony.conf on node2 rewritten to use only 'server 10.100.95.10 iburst prefer'; chronyc sources shows node2 selected (^*) node1 as its time source, reaching stratum 4 with Normal leap status

evidence.requirement: Bidirectional verification of the node1<->node2 time relationship
evidence.summary: chronyc clients on node1 shows node2 (10.100.95.11) issuing NTP requests, both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 95ac0c32...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 563c378f... (changed) with uptime 16s; chronyd auto-started, config persisted, resynced to pool and still serving allow rule for the cluster

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ce1f9012... synced to node1; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id ba190ddb... (changed) with uptime 16s; chronyd auto-started, config persisted (server 10.100.95.10 prefer), and re-selected (^*) node1 as source at stratum 5
